heading: GPT-2 small’s 26-head, seven-class IOI circuit is faithful, complete and minimal
definition: GPT-2 small does IOI through 26 attention heads in 7 classes (e.g. duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover heads), meeting faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
summary: In indirect object identification (IOI), the model predicts the recipient’s name; independent studies support several circuit components, but contest whether the proposed circuit fully explains this behavior. Stricter tests find connections that can be removed and task-relevant information outside the circuit; how well the circuit reproduces model behavior depends on evaluation methods, and one pathway’s effect changes direction.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for the full V1 conjunction at <1B; R1 for ACDC's partial recovery of canonical heads in GPT-2 small, given author overlap with an original source (arXiv:2304.14997#r25). No V1 status established at other scales; counts versions.V1.studies_by_size is predominantly 'not stated'.
suggested_status.reason: The full wording is contested by a reversed pathway effect and by qualified faithfulness and minimality results. MURANO reverses the L9H6 query-patch effect (arXiv:2608.30662#r12); stricter testing finds removable edges and remaining complement information (arXiv:2410.13032#R2; arXiv:2410.13032#R7); faithfulness evaluation is method-sensitive (arXiv:2407.08734#R5; arXiv:2407.08734#R12). ACDC recovers nine canonical heads using an alternative automated discovery procedure (arXiv:2304.14997#r25), but the checker records an author shared with an original source; this supports R1 partial reproduction, not an independent R2 classification. counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 31; versions.V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 17; versions.V1.verdicts.challenges.studies = 1. These are overlapping verdict categories, not votes on the complete conjunction. Scale coverage follows versions.V1.studies_by_size; author-overlap caution follows versions.V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original.
suggested_status.open_questions: An external rerun of the complete original protocol could establish how much of the exact inventory and original criteria reproduces jointly. Matched implementations and prompt sets could determine whether the L9H6 reversal persists. Template- and error-stratified validation could establish what the circuit explains beyond pooled successful predictions.

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: Wang et al. studied IOI in GPT-2 small using path patching (replacing signals along chosen connections) and attention-head ablations (removing head contributions).
original_result.result: The proposed circuit retained 87% of the full model’s mean logit difference—the average output-score margin for the recipient’s name over the subject’s name—and random and whole-class removals produced small discrepancies between circuit and full-model responses to those removals. Greedy searches for removal sets found discrepancies up to 3.09, compared with the original logit difference of 3.56. In the minimality tests, removing each of its 26 heads, after removing a chosen set of other heads, changed the logit difference by at least 1% of the original logit difference.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Attribution-score signs matched the proposed name-mover and negative-name-mover roles.
Feature circuits recovered several proposed head classes with partial overlap in individual heads.
Subject-inhibition heads wrote a position signal mediated through name-mover queries.
Removing name-mover input eliminated negative heads' preference between the two names.
The base IOI circuit retained most model performance under mean ablation.
Automated discovery selected nine heads from the original IOI circuit.
Contextual decomposition recovered six proposed IOI head classes among its most relevant nodes.
The IOI circuit outperformed random circuits in faithfulness and knockout tests.
Parameter analysis identified name copying and suppression consistent with the proposed head roles.
Interventions on traced subject-inhibition connections changed IOI performance in the predicted directions.
The manual circuit was approximately optimal under optimized ablation.
Decoded activations matched proposed name and position content across most tested circuit heads.
English IOI path patching recovered a circuit resembling the original, including negative name movers.
Component interventions traced how duplicate-token and subject-inhibition signals control name-mover attention.
Patching recovered expected name-mover heads and late subject-to-output information flow.
The strongest patching effects came from proposed name-mover, backup and subject-inhibition heads.
Under subject-swapped patching, the canonical IOI circuit exceeded the full model's score gap between names.
Subject-inhibition heads carried both position and token signals, with position dominant.
Token decomposition recovered proposed circuit roles and their sensitivity to the tested corruption.
Head patching reproduced the expected positive and negative name-mover effects.
Head sweeps and query patches reproduced several name-mover and subject-inhibition effects.
Name-mover output swaps produced the predicted answers in nearly all tested pairs.
The manual circuit closely matched average performance and correct answers under two ablation methods.
Qualitative patching recovered the proposed information paths between IOI head classes.
Position-direction patching altered IOI predictions while whole-MLP8 patching had no effect.
Changing subject order redirected subject-inhibition signals and name-mover attention, usually flipping the answer.
Swap graphs recovered name and position signals linking subject-inhibition to name movers.
Attention layer 8 made the largest positive contribution to the IOI score gap between names.
Path patching linked three induction features to subject-inhibition head values.
Duplicate-token heads detected incidental duplication while name movers still mainly attended to IO.
The published circuit reproduced intact-model answers on nearly all held-out prompts of the tested pattern.
Single name-mover directions flipped fewer than half of IOI predictions.
With the tested resampling scheme, only about 79% of the model's score gap between names remained.
Some nodes outside the circuit had stronger causal effects than most circuit nodes.
Contextual decomposition recovered a different head set and only three backup name movers.
Stringent tests found failures of equivalence, independence and edge-level minimality.
Sparse tracing recovered only part of the circuit; intervening on a head reversed the expected effects.
Smaller optimized circuits substantially outperformed the manual circuit under several ablation methods.
Two duplicate-token heads encoded subject names rather than the hypothesized position signal.
Selected components reproduced only part of subject-inhibition behavior.
IOI circuit faithfulness varied substantially across ablation methods and individual prompts.
Mean ablation of all three name movers left the IOI score gap between names essentially unchanged.
Subject-inhibition variable swaps produced predicted answers in only part of the tested pairs.
The circuit poorly reproduced model errors and lost faithfulness under resample ablation.
Causal scrubbing recovered much less of the IOI score gap between names than mean ablation.
A proposed backup name mover instead acted as a gender head.
On the tested prompt pattern, subject-inhibition partly increased indirect-object attention rather than suppressing the subject.
Duplicating IO did not trigger the general duplicate-removal behavior described by the algorithm.
Patching a head's query changed the score gap between names opposite to predicted subject suppression.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A complete external rerun of the original joint validation protocol: the exact head inventory, causal roles of every class, original faithfulness, subset-based completeness and subset-conditioned head minimality in the same unchanged model and prompt setup.
untested.basis: Inferred coverage gap, not an explicit disclaimer in arXiv:2304.14997 or arXiv:2411.16105. arXiv:2304.14997 reports automated circuit recovery, canonical edge/node ROC AUC and canonical-circuit logit difference (including arXiv:2304.14997#r25 and arXiv:2304.14997#r26). arXiv:2411.16105 evaluates base-circuit faithfulness (arXiv:2411.16105#r4, arXiv:2411.16105#r7), selected head functions and variant circuits. Neither reports the complete joint rerun. arXiv:2410.13032 uses different edge-level minimality tests (arXiv:2410.13032#R3, arXiv:2410.13032#R7). counts: versions.V1.main_rows_by_operation records component operations but has no joint-protocol coverage key; that absence alone does not establish the gap. Individual criteria and selected classes are tested elsewhere in this synthesis.

untested.what: Template-stratified validation that the exact circuit jointly meets all original criteria, including on model-error cases.
untested.basis: The original baseline is pooled over templates and orders (arXiv:2211.00593#r1). The error-agreement evaluation is also pooled and does not rerun original completeness or minimality (arXiv:2609.35686#r1). counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation has no template-stratified joint-validation field. Selected prompt variants and error mechanisms have been tested, so those are not general gaps.

wording_issues.issue: This names the proposed reference inventory rather than a uniquely recovered or universally necessary set. ACDC selects a sufficient subset within it; CD-T recovers different membership. Singular-vector tracing's skeleton, filtered at approximately 170 occurrences, contains 21 heads, including 11 of 16 eligible reference heads. Some outside nodes have appreciable causal effects.

Broad functional classes recur, but particular head interpretations differ. InversionView decodes subject-name content rather than the hypothesized position signal in duplicate-token heads 0.1 and 0.10; swap graphs identify a gender-related role for a reported backup head.

The label needs a specified target, pathway and prompt condition. L9H6 query patching reverses the expected effect in MURANO; BABA feature analysis includes IO boosting; incidental duplicate prompts suggest a position-specific role.

Faithfulness requires its metric, replacement distribution, granularity and averaging convention. The original reports 87% of full-model mean logit difference; later evaluations show prompt variability, overshoot and low agreement on model errors despite high average task faithfulness.

The original criteria are operational and qualified by subset search. They should not imply equivalence, absence of task information outside the circuit or edge-level irreducibility: later statistical tests reject these stronger properties, while optimized alternatives depend strongly on ablation convention.

method_sensitivity.what: Within the same pooled evaluation, mean, ABC-resample and optimal ablation give normalized faithfulness 0.956, 0.644 and 0.906, respectively. Exact error agreement changes to 15.2%, 40.6% and 10.0%. The optimal-ablation comparison also changes how close the manual circuit appears to optimized alternatives.

method_sensitivity.factor: Node, edge and path intervention scope
method_sensitivity.what: For GPT-2 small IOI, edge-level token-specific ablation produces median recovery well above 100%, without an exact numerical median reported. Path-based causal scrubbing gives much lower and noisy recovery than the original node-mean-ablation baseline. Local ablation of incoming signals to (9,6) increases the IO logit, whereas global ablation decreases it; local boosting decreases the IO logit. These local effects reverse the expected V1 direction while demonstrating the intervention sensitivity described by V5.

For selected GPT-2 small IOI representations, inhibition-channel patching gives 97.5% fractional logit difference decrease but 35% interchange accuracy. A DAS residual direction gives 140.7% fractional logit difference decrease and 74.8% interchange accuracy; a name-mover-gradient direction gives 111.5% and 45.1%, respectively. Large logit changes do not imply corresponding hard-answer interchange success. These component and single-direction interventions do not evaluate the full 26-head circuit's sufficiency, completeness or minimality.

For GPT-2 small IOI, MURANO's query patch lowers logit difference by 28.9% of the clean-to-corrupt gap for L9H9 and 22.8% for L10H0, but raises it by 4.9% for L9H6. Rank-one component editing also differs across S-inhibition heads: the proposed 7.3 component has little effect, while other reported component removals reduce inhibition. The component-editing results concern selected communication components and do not test the full circuit's completeness or minimality.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prompt distribution, name order and corruption
method_sensitivity.what: The S-inhibition interpretation changes between ABBA and BABA feature analyses. On incidental-duplicate prompts, duplicate-token heads respond to the duplicate, while S-inhibition heads mostly attend to S2 and two shift toward the duplicate; these are attention observations, with no patching or logit decoding establishing inhibition. In a separate GPT-2 small layer-level patching study, attention layer 8 matters under both switched-name corruption and third-name counterexamples, with the highest importance difference and greater importance for third-name counterexamples. That study's S-inhibition interpretation is circumstantial; it does not isolate the claimed heads or test V1's circuit criteria.

method_sensitivity.factor: Completeness search and definition of minimality
method_sensitivity.what: The original header reports larger incompleteness under greedy search than random or whole-class subset sampling. Later edge-level testing finds removable edges under a different minimality definition. Subset-conditioned head contributions and edge-level irreducibility answer different questions.
